getting_started.title: 🎓 Welcome to Your Admin Panel!
getting_started.intro: This is your personal dashboard to manage everything on your portfolio website. Don't worry — I'll guide you through every section step by step.

steps.title: 1. Start with your Profile
steps.desc: Go to Profile and fill in your name, title, bio, and links. This is what visitors see first on your site.

steps.title: 2. Add your Skills
steps.desc: Go to Skills and add the technologies you know. Set a proficiency level (0-100%) for each one.

steps.title: 3. Create a Contract
steps.desc: Go to Contracts and create a contract for each client project. Add the client name, amount, and dates.

steps.title: 4. Add a Project
steps.desc: Go to Projects and create a new project. Link it to a contract, describe what you built, and mark it as Featured to show it on your landing page.

steps.title: 5. Track Progress with Phases
steps.desc: Inside each project, click 'Phases' to add stages like Design, Development, Testing. Update progress as you work.

steps.title: 6. Check Messages
steps.desc: Go to Messages to read contact form submissions from visitors. Mark them as read when you've responded.

dashboard.title: 📊 Dashboard — Your Overview
dashboard.what: The Dashboard shows you a quick summary of everything in your portfolio.
how: Each card shows a count: how many projects, skills, unread messages, and testimonials you have.
If there are unresolved errors, you'll see a red warning box — click 'View Errors' to investigate.
Use the quick action buttons to jump directly to Profile, SQL Scripts, Messages, or Error Logs.
tips: Check the Dashboard first whenever you log in — it tells you what needs attention.
Green checkmark means everything is running smoothly.
Red warning means there's an error that needs your attention.

profile.title: 👤 Profile — Your Identity
profile.what: This is where you define who you are. Everything here appears on your public landing page.

how.desc: Your complete name — e.g., 'Mahbod Pour'
Your job title — e.g., 'Frontend Developer & UI/UX Enthusiast'
Three lines of text that appear in the hero section. The third line will be gold and italic.
A paragraph about yourself — your experience, passion, and what you do.
Your email, location, LinkedIn, GitHub, Twitter — these appear in the footer.
This is how Google sees your site. Write a short description (150-160 characters) and keywords. The OG Image is what shows when someone shares your site link.
Your changes go live immediately on the website!

tips: The Meta Description is very important for Google — make it compelling!
Keep the tagline short and impactful — visitors read this first.
Update your profile photo URL if you have one.

projects.title: 📁 Projects — Your Work Showcase
projects.what: Projects are pieces of work you've done. Featured projects appear on your landing page as playing-card style previews.

how.desc: Start by creating a new project.
Title is the project name. Slug is the URL-friendly version (e.g., 'my-project').
Pick a category (Web App, SaaS, Design) and enter the client name.
One line that summarizes what the project is about.
A detailed paragraph about what you built, technologies used, and the outcome.
Enter as JSON — e.g., ["Blazor","SQL Server","Chart.js"]
Link to a contract you've created — this connects the project to a client.
Choose how the preview card looks: Dark (dark UI), Light (bright UI), or Brand (logo + colors).
How the card tilts on the page — try '-6deg', '3deg', or '-2deg'.
Turn ON to show this project on your landing page. Only 3 projects are shown.
Turn ON when you're ready for the world to see it. Turn OFF to hide it.

tips: Only Featured projects appear on the landing page — mark your 3 best ones!
After creating a project, click '📊 Phases' to track your progress step by step.
The mockup style changes how the card looks — experiment to find the best fit.

contracts.title: 📋 Contracts — Client Agreements
contracts.what: Contracts are agreements with clients. You can track client names, project amounts, and contract status.

how.desc: Create a new contract for a client project.
A descriptive name for the contract — e.g., 'Website Redesign for TechCorp'.
Pending = not started yet. Active = working on it. Completed = done. Cancelled = didn't happen.
Who this contract is for.
The project value — in EUR, USD, or IRR.
When the project starts and ends.
Any extra details about the agreement or special notes.

tips: Link contracts to projects in the Projects section — this connects everything together.
Use the Status field to track which contracts are active vs completed.
The client name will appear on the project card in the admin panel.

phases.title: 📊 Phases — Track Project Progress
phases.what: Phases break a project into smaller steps. Each phase has its own progress percentage.

how.desc: Add a new phase to your project — e.g., 'Design', 'Development', 'Testing', 'Launch'.
The name of the phase.
Pending = not started. In Progress = working on it. Completed = done. On Hold = paused.
How much of this phase is complete — 0% to 100%. The overall progress bar at the top shows the average of all phases.
When you plan to start and finish this phase.

tips: Keep phases small and focused — it's easier to track progress.
Update the progress percentage regularly to see your project moving forward.
The overall progress bar gives you a quick view of how the project is going.

skills.title: ⚡ Skills — Your Toolkit
skills.what: Skills show visitors what technologies and tools you know. They appear as progress bars and tag labels on your landing page.

how.desc: Create a new skill entry.
The technology name — e.g., 'C# / .NET', 'React', 'Docker'.
Group it — e.g., 'Frontend', 'Backend', 'Database', 'DevOps'.
How good you are (0-100). This creates the progress bar on your site.
Skill Bar = shows a progress bar with percentage. Tag = shows as a simple label (for things like Git, Figma, Azure).

tips: Use Skill Bars for your main technologies (the ones with progress bars).
Use Tags for tools and platforms that don't need a percentage.
Order matters — skills appear in the order you create them.

experiences.title: 💼 Experiences — Your Work History
experiences.what: Experiences show your career timeline on the 'About Me' section of your landing page.

how.desc: Add a new work experience.
Where you worked and your job title.
What you did there — key achievements and responsibilities.
Leave End Date empty if you still work there — it will show 'Present'.

tips: List experiences from most recent to oldest.
Keep descriptions concise and achievement-focused.
Leave End Date empty for your current job.

testimonials.title: 💬 Testimonials — What People Say
testimonials.what: Testimonials are quotes from clients or colleagues. They appear in the contact section of your landing page as a rotating carousel.

how.desc: Add a new testimonial.
Who said it — e.g., 'Alex Schmidt, CTO at TechCorp'.
The quote itself — keep it genuine and impactful.
1 to 5 stars — 5 is the best.

tips: Ask real clients for quotes — authentic testimonials build trust.
Keep testimonials focused on results and collaboration.
The carousel rotates automatically every 4.5 seconds on the landing page.

messages.title: ✉️ Messages — Contact Form Submissions
messages.what: When someone fills out the contact form on your website, their message appears here.

how.desc: Click 'All' to see everything, or 'Unread' to see only new messages.
Click 'Mark Read' after you've responded to the sender.
Remove messages you no longer need.

tips: Check this section regularly — visitors might be reaching out with project opportunities!
The Dashboard shows you how many unread messages you have.
Respond to messages via email — the sender's email is shown on each message.

resources.title: 🗄️ Resources — SQL Script Runner
resources.what: This is where you execute SQL scripts that set up and maintain your database.

how.desc: Each file is a database script. Click to execute it.
Executes all scripts in order (01 → 02 → 03 → 04 → 05).
The table on the right shows which files ran successfully (✓ OK) and which failed (✗ ERROR).
If a file failed, hover over the error column to see what went wrong.

tips: Scripts run automatically when the API starts — you usually don't need to run them manually.
Only run files if you've added new SQL scripts or need to re-run a failed one.
Files are named 01-, 02-, etc. — they must run in order.

errors.title: 🔍 Error Logs — Find & Fix Problems
errors.what: This shows every error that happened in your application. Use it to understand what went wrong and when.

how.desc: Click 'All' to see everything. 'Errors' for critical issues. 'Warnings' for less serious. 'Unresolved' for things that still need attention.
Each entry shows: what happened (Message), where it happened (Source), when (Timestamp), and which page (Request Path).
Click 'Stack Trace' to see the technical details — useful for developers debugging issues.
Click ✓ after you've fixed the problem. This marks it as resolved.
If you've fixed everything, click 'Resolve All' to mark all as done.
Remove all error logs — use this when you want a fresh start.

tips: The Dashboard warns you when there are unresolved errors — check it regularly.
Stack traces are technical — share them with your developer if you need help.
Resolving errors doesn't delete them — it just marks them as handled.
